about: The interior of the right lung: three lobes, the airway tree, the pulmonary arteries and veins, alveolar clusters and the pleura. The branching is a deterministic illustration of three divisions per lobe, not a traced bronchial atlas, the alveoli are drawn many times life size, and nothing here models gas exchange itself; activity is a display index of the engine's own breathing and circulation signals.

parts.label: Upper Lobe
parts.summary: Right upper lobe, above the horizontal fissure
parts.function: The right upper lobe lies above the horizontal fissure and takes in the apex of the lung beneath the collarbone. It is supplied by its own lobar bronchus, artery and vein. Air reaches it through its own lobar bronchus. It brightens when breathing is deeper or faster, for example when the exercise level is raised, and dims when breathing is depressed.

drives.note: A lobe is ventilated in proportion to the breathing the body is doing.
Shallow or slow breathing leaves the lobe less ventilated than at rest.

parts.label: Middle Lobe
parts.summary: Right middle lobe, a wedge between the two fissures
parts.function: The middle lobe is a small wedge on the front of the right lung, between the horizontal and oblique fissures. Only the right lung has one; the left lung's lingula is its counterpart. Air reaches it through its own lobar bronchus. It brightens when breathing is deeper or faster, for example when the exercise level is raised, and dims when breathing is depressed.

drives.note: A lobe is ventilated in proportion to the breathing the body is doing.
Shallow or slow breathing leaves the lobe less ventilated than at rest.

parts.label: Lower Lobe
parts.summary: Right lower lobe, below the oblique fissure
parts.function: The lower lobe is the largest and lies below and behind the oblique fissure, resting on the diaphragm. In an upright body most of the breath is drawn into the lower lobes. Air reaches it through its own lobar bronchus. It brightens when breathing is deeper or faster, for example when the exercise level is raised, and dims when breathing is depressed.

drives.note: A lobe is ventilated in proportion to the breathing the body is doing.
Shallow or slow breathing leaves the lobe less ventilated than at rest.

parts.label: Bronchial Tree
parts.summary: Lobar bronchi dividing into ever smaller airways
parts.function: The main bronchus divides into lobar bronchi, which divide again and again until the air reaches the terminal airways. These tubes carry air but do not exchange gas, so they make up the anatomical dead space. Air runs in from the hilum while the lung fills and back out while it empties; the stream stops in apnoea, thins when the airways narrow, and the tree takes a warm tint.

drives.note: More air moves through the airways when minute ventilation rises.
Airway narrowing is a direct property of the bronchial smooth muscle.

parts.label: Pulmonary Arteries
parts.summary: Carry oxygen-poor blood from the right heart to the alveoli
parts.function: The pulmonary artery branches alongside the airways and carries all of the cardiac output, oxygen-poor blood from the right ventricle, out to the capillaries around the alveoli. In this view the blood is drawn in the venous colour and moves faster when cardiac output is higher; it stops if the heart stops.

drives.note: The whole cardiac output passes through the lungs, so more flow when output rises.

parts.label: Pulmonary Veins
parts.summary: Carry oxygenated blood back to the left atrium
parts.function: The pulmonary veins run between the lung segments, away from the airways, and return freshly oxygenated blood to the left atrium. The stream is drawn in the colour of arterial blood, so it pales towards purple as the oxygen saturation falls.

drives.note: Venous return from the lungs follows cardiac output.
With less oxygen taken up, the blood returning has less oxygen to carry.

parts.label: Alveoli
parts.summary: Air sacs where oxygen and carbon dioxide are exchanged
parts.function: Each smallest airway ends in a cluster of alveoli, thin-walled sacs wrapped in capillaries, where oxygen passes into the blood and carbon dioxide passes out. They are drawn far larger than life so the clusters can be seen. They brighten with each inspiration, and dim where blood passes through unventilated lung, which is what a shunt is.

drives.note: Alveolar ventilation is what refreshes the gas in the sacs.
Low arterial oxygen is the signal that the exchange surface is being asked to work harder.
Blood that passes unventilated lung does not take part in exchange.

parts.label: Pleura
parts.summary: The smooth membrane that wraps the lung
parts.function: The visceral pleura covers the lung surface and slides against the lining of the chest wall on a thin film of fluid, which lets the lung follow the chest as it expands. It has no drive of its own in this simulation and is shown for orientation.

parts.label: Apex
parts.summary: Rounded top of the lung
parts.function: The apex rises above the first rib into the root of the neck and is covered by pleura. It is the part of the lung that moves least when the chest wall expands.

drives.note: This surface moves with the breath, so it works harder when breathing is deeper or faster.

parts.label: Costal Surface
parts.summary: Rib-facing surface, smooth and convex
parts.function: It lies against the ribs and intercostal muscles with only the pleura between. Its shape follows the inside of the chest wall, so it moves outward as the ribs lift in breathing.

drives.note: This surface moves with the breath, so it works harder when breathing is deeper or faster.

parts.label: Mediastinal Surface
parts.summary: Surface facing the central compartment of the chest
parts.function: It is moulded by the heart, great vessels and oesophagus, and the structures of the lung root enter and leave on it. On the right it carries the groove for the oesophagus and the large veins.

parts.label: Diaphragmatic Surface
parts.summary: Concave base resting on the diaphragm
parts.function: The base of the lung sits on the dome of the diaphragm, so it is pulled downward when the diaphragm contracts and the lung fills with air.

drives.note: This surface moves with the breath, so it works harder when breathing is deeper or faster.

parts.label: Oblique Fissure
parts.summary: Deep cleft that separates the lower lobe from the other two
parts.function: The oblique fissure runs from high behind to low in front. It separates the right lower lobe from the upper and middle lobes, and lets each lobe slide against the next as it expands.

parts.label: Horizontal Fissure
parts.summary: Cleft between the right upper and middle lobes
parts.function: The horizontal fissure runs forward from the oblique fissure to the front border of the lung. It separates the right upper lobe from the middle lobe and can be incomplete.

parts.label: Hilum (Root of the Lung)
parts.summary: Where the airway and vessels enter the lung
parts.function: The hilum is the opening on the mediastinal surface through which the main bronchus, the pulmonary artery and veins, the bronchial vessels, nerves and lymphatics pass. Together these structures form the root of the lung.

drives.note: All of the blood flow to and from the lung passes through the root.

parts.label: Pulmonary Ligament
parts.summary: Fold of pleura hanging below the lung root
parts.function: A double sheet of pleura hangs below the root of the lung and joins the lower lung to the mediastinum. It anchors the lower lung while allowing the root to move.

parts.label: Bronchial Arteries
parts.summary: Small arteries that nourish the airway wall
parts.function: They arise from the aorta or its branches and run along the bronchi, supplying the bronchial walls, the connective tissue and the pleura. The alveoli are supplied instead by the pulmonary circulation.

drives.note: Systemic arterial flow to the airway wall follows cardiac output.

parts.label: Bronchial Veins
parts.summary: Small veins that drain the airway wall
parts.function: Those near the root of the lung drain into the azygos system. The rest drain into the pulmonary veins, so a little unoxygenated blood joins the oxygenated blood returning to the heart.

drives.note: Venous return from the airway wall follows cardiac output.

parts.label: Hilar Lymph Nodes
parts.summary: Lymph nodes gathered at the lung root
parts.function: Lymph from the lung drains first along the bronchi and then to the nodes at the hilum. The nodes filter it on its way to the mediastinum.

drives.note: Nodes draining an infected area become more active.

parts.label: Visceral Pleura
parts.summary: Pleura that covers the lung itself
parts.function: The visceral layer is a thin membrane stuck to the surface of the lung, and it dips into the fissures between the lobes. It is continuous at the root with the parietal layer.

parts.label: Parietal Pleura
parts.summary: Pleura that lines the chest wall
parts.function: The parietal layer lines the inside of the chest wall, the diaphragm and the sides of the mediastinum. It is the outer wall of the pleural cavity and is sensitive to pain.

parts.label: Pleural Cavity
parts.summary: Thin space between the two layers of pleura
parts.function: The cavity is a potential space holding only a thin film of fluid. The fluid lets the lung slide on the chest wall, and the pull between the layers keeps the lung expanded against the wall.

parts.label: Costodiaphragmatic Recess
parts.summary: Lower pocket of the pleural cavity
parts.function: Below the lung, where the parietal pleura turns from the chest wall onto the diaphragm, the cavity forms a recess that the lung enters only in deep inspiration.

parts.label: Main Bronchus
parts.summary: The primary bronchus entering the lung
parts.function: The windpipe divides at the carina into a right and a left main bronchus, and each enters its lung at the hilum. The right main bronchus is wider, shorter and more vertical than the left.

drives.note: More air moves through the airway when minute ventilation rises.
Smooth muscle narrows the airway wall.

parts.label: Lobar Bronchi
parts.summary: One bronchus for each lobe
parts.function: The main bronchus divides into a lobar bronchus for every lobe of the lung. Each lobar bronchus then divides into segmental bronchi.

drives.note: More air moves through the airway when minute ventilation rises.
Smooth muscle narrows the airway wall.

parts.label: Segmental Bronchi
parts.summary: One bronchus for each bronchopulmonary segment
parts.function: Each segmental bronchus supplies one bronchopulmonary segment and runs with its own branch of the pulmonary artery. Their walls still contain cartilage.

drives.note: More air moves through the airway when minute ventilation rises.
Smooth muscle narrows the airway wall.

parts.label: Bronchioles
parts.summary: Small airways without cartilage
parts.function: Bronchioles have no cartilage in their walls, so their width is controlled by smooth muscle and held open by the pull of the surrounding lung. They narrow when the muscle contracts in bronchoconstriction.

drives.note: More air moves through the airway when minute ventilation rises.
Smooth muscle narrows the airway wall.

parts.label: Terminal Bronchioles
parts.summary: The last airways that only carry air
parts.function: The terminal bronchioles are the final purely conducting airways. Beyond them the airway gains alveoli in its wall, and their lining contains club cells rather than goblet cells.

drives.note: More air moves through the airway when minute ventilation rises.
Smooth muscle narrows the airway wall.

parts.label: Respiratory Bronchioles
parts.summary: First airways with alveoli in their walls
parts.function: Alveoli open directly from the wall of a respiratory bronchiole, so it carries air and also takes part in gas exchange. It leads on to the alveolar ducts.

drives.note: Alveolar ventilation refreshes the air at the start of the exchange zone.

parts.label: Alveolar Ducts
parts.summary: Passages lined by openings into alveoli
parts.function: An alveolar duct is an airway whose wall is almost all openings into alveoli. It ends in alveolar sacs.

parts.label: Alveolar Sacs
parts.summary: Clusters of alveoli at the end of a duct
parts.function: An alveolar sac is a group of alveoli that share one opening from an alveolar duct. Most gas exchange takes place in the sacs.

parts.label: Type I Pneumocytes
parts.summary: Thin, flat cells that form the alveolar surface
parts.function: These cells are extremely thin so that gases cross them quickly. They form the air side of the respiratory membrane.

parts.label: Type II Pneumocytes
parts.summary: Cells that make surfactant
parts.function: They make and release surfactant, which lowers the surface tension of the alveolar lining and helps keep the alveoli from collapsing. They can also divide to replace type I cells.

parts.label: Alveolar Macrophages
parts.summary: Scavenger cells of the air spaces
parts.function: They engulf inhaled dust and microbes that reach the alveoli. Many are then carried up the airway on the mucus or leave through the lymphatics.

drives.note: These cells are recruited and activated by infection.

parts.label: Alveolar Capillaries
parts.summary: Capillary network wrapped round each alveolus
parts.function: Blood from the pulmonary arteries passes through them in a thin sheet beside the alveolar air. Oxygen crosses into the blood and carbon dioxide crosses out.

drives.note: The whole cardiac output passes through the lungs, so flow rises with output.

parts.label: Respiratory Membrane
parts.summary: The thin barrier that gases cross
parts.function: Gas crosses the alveolar lining cell, the fused basement membranes and the capillary lining cell. Because the barrier is so thin, oxygen and carbon dioxide diffuse across it quickly.

drives.note: Blood that bypasses ventilated alveoli does not cross the membrane.

parts.label: Alveolar Pores (of Kohn)
parts.summary: Small openings between neighbouring alveoli
parts.function: The pores let air pass between adjacent alveoli. This lets an alveolus be ventilated through its neighbours if its own airway is blocked.

parts.label: Apical Segment
parts.summary: Bronchopulmonary segment of the right upper lobe
parts.function: Each bronchopulmonary segment has its own segmental bronchus and its own branch of the pulmonary artery, and is separated from its neighbours by connective tissue. It works as a separate unit of the lung.

drives.note: A segment is ventilated in proportion to the breathing the body is doing.

parts.summary: Bronchopulmonary segment of the right upper lobe
parts.function: Each bronchopulmonary segment has its own segmental bronchus and its own branch of the pulmonary artery, and is separated from its neighbours by connective tissue. It works as a separate unit of the lung.

drives.note: A segment is ventilated in proportion to the breathing the body is doing.
